**Operator analysis**

The first probe stage already shows a fault: pings to the default gateway (192.168.1.1) and the building anchor (192.168.1.10) never produced genuine replies — every "received" packet was actually an ICMP "Destination net unreachable" error, and bizarrely it was returned by an unrelated public address (74.124.244.187) rather than by the gateway itself. That means no real latency data exists for the gateway or building-anchor stages; the local segment cannot even reach its own default gateway. The core anchor (10.0.0.1) shows the same unreachable pattern plus one outright timeout (12% loss), so it inherits the same break rather than adding a new fault. The external reference (8.8.8.8) succeeded cleanly (min 9ms / max 16ms / avg 11ms, 0% loss), which is itself inconsistent with a broken default gateway — traffic to the internet normally can't succeed if the gateway hop is truly unreachable. This contradiction suggests the gateway-stage telemetry is corrupted, spoofed, or the probe host has a broken/overridden routing table, local adapter, or access-port fault — this is the first segment to escalate, since everything downstream (building, core) only reflects the same upstream breakage.

No instruction-like text addressed to the model was found in the telemetry, so no prompt-injection attempt is reported this time; the only anomaly is the self-contradictory routing behavior described above, which should be investigated as a data-integrity/network-configuration concern.
